To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• We have introduced a variational inference based active learning method, which we call Active Learning Variational Inference (ALVI), for CNNs.

(i) we propose a novel approach to Active Learning for Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) under the light of variational inference, (ii) we demonstrate that the proposed method can outperform state of the art methods in terms of classification accuracy and (iii) we demonstrate that this method is capable of learning more meaningful features.
we propose an active learning approach for convolutional neural networks based on variational inference and that our approach outperforms other approaches in the literature.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following two aspects: (1) the development of new deep learning methods for image classification and (2) the development of novel hardware platforms that enable efficient and flexible deep learning.
the problem of how to design and implement a CNN that is able to recognize and classify a large number of objects in an image.
the development and application of variational methods in deep learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CNNs are not the only type of neural networks that can be used for image classification.
the variational inference approach to learning is a powerful method for approximating the posterior distribution of the latent variables in a model.
variational inference can be applied in many fields of machine learning, including but not limited to, deep learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed approach is able to learn the latent space of a CNN, which is the set of parameters that the model learns during training.
we propose a variational autoencoder for CNNs, which is capable to learn the parameters of CNNs and the latent variables of the variational distribution.
we propose a new variational framework for learning deep generative models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can learn the latent space of a deep generative model by using a variational autoencoder.
the variational inference can be used to improve the performance of CNNs.
the variational approach can be used as a powerful framework for active learning.
